title: Two field extensions embed in a common field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension] and let $E/k$ and $F/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Then there exists a field $M$ [def-pc-field-extension] and $k$-field embeddings $E\to M$ and $F\to M$.

proof.text: Put $T=E\otimes_k F$. The algebra maps from $k$ into the fields $E$ and $F$ are injective, and the fields are domains. Apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-tensor-nontrivial] (Algebra.TensorProduct.nontrivial_of_algebraMap_injective_of_isDomain) to make $T$ nontrivial; injectivity of the tensor-factor inclusions is not needed.

Choose a maximal ideal $I$ of $T$ by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal], implemented directly with Ideal.exists_maximal, and set $M=T/I$. Install the field structure Ideal.Quotient.field I by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field]; the quotient carries its canonical $k$-algebra structure.

source.place: Fields, Lemma 9.2, tag 0H7K (take a residue field of the tensor product)

proof.text: Compose Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ k I with Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft and includeRight to obtain $k$-algebra homomorphisms $i:E\to M$ and $j:F\to M$. Homomorphisms from fields to a nontrivial ring are injective (AlgHom.injective): a nonzero element in a kernel would have an inverse, forcing $1=0$. The quotient type lives in universe max(v,w), so these maps give the required existential witness.

proof_origin.place: Fields, Lemma 9.2, tag 0H7K (tensor product and maximal-ideal quotient; direct Mathlib implementation, factor-inclusion injectivity omitted)

split_report.summary: Split the common-overfield lemma through the tensor product: the field factors inject into and make the tensor product nontrivial, a maximal ideal exists, and its quotient is a field; the induced unital maps from each factor are injective.

lean.statement: theorem exists_common_extension (k : Type u) (E : Type v) (F : Type w) [Field k] [Field E] [Field F] [Algebra k E] [Algebra k F] : ∃ (M : Type (max v w)) (_ : Field M) (_ : Algebra k M) (i : E →ₐ[k] M) (j : F →ₐ[k] M), Function.Injective i ∧ Function.Injective j
